Oxagen house system v2.5

One house.
Two names. One gold.

Everything a customer sees from Oxagen and Stella comes from one system: obsidian and white, three faces, and a single gold that each name carries in exactly one glyph.

The decision

The house kit

The Oxagen brand kit already had the right bones: Space Grotesk and a wordmark whose only colour is one gold letter. This system takes that kit as the base and brings Stella onto it. Since September 2026 it sits on obsidian #09090B and white, with neutral greys between, so the gold is the only warm value on a screen.

oxagen is the kit's wordmark, reproduced from the font: the word in Space Grotesk 600, lowercase, its x in gold. stella* is the same word treatment followed by the font's own asterisk, in the same gold. The asterisk is a character, not a drawing; it was never redrawn, and it must not be.

The gold is #D4AF37. Both names use it at the same value, so the two marks cannot drift apart.

  • One glyph is gold. The x in oxagen, the asterisk in stella. Never a second one.
  • Gold is identity, and one action per screen. It is never a surface, and it never means a state.
  • Gold as text on paper becomes gold-deep. The mark keeps its metal; words do not.
  • Nothing sits to the left of stella. The asterisk is the only mark. Oxagen's lockup is the one exception, and only for Oxagen.
  • The hive is two colours, and only two. Its outlines take the colour of whatever it sits on -- paper on ink, ink on paper, currentColor in the adaptive files -- and its two lit cells take the metal. Nothing else in it is ever coloured, and a mono file paints all of it one colour.
  • The icon is the only picture we own. No stock illustration, no gradient mesh, no 3D render. A surface that needs a picture builds one out of the icon -- its outline, its mosaic, a field around it -- or simply uses a bigger one.

Logos

Wordmarks

Both are set at the same size, 131.7 px per em, the size the kit's oxagen outline was frozen at. Each sits in an ink-tight box, so oxagen (454×93) and stella* (406×94) are the same height to within a pixel and the same letter size exactly.

The asterisk

Space Grotesk's asterisk is a six-armed, cap-height glyph, 59 units square at the logo em. It sits where the font puts it after an a, with no added space and no kerning. It is the same glyph in the wordmark, the icon, the favicon and the wallpaper.

Variants

The oxagen lockup

Oxagen alone has a lockup: the hive, a gap, then the word. The hive stands a quarter taller than the wordmark's box and centres on it; the gap is a little over half an x-height. The wordmark on its own is still the preferred mark -- the lockup is for the places that want a picture beside the name, a masthead or an app's title bar. Stella has no lockup; its asterisk is already in the word.

Minimum sizes

Wordmark 88 px wide on screen, 24 mm in print. Icon 24 px, 8 mm. Lockup 120 px, 32 mm. Below that, use the favicon.

Misuse

Icons

The asterisk and the hive

Where a square is required, Stella uses its asterisk and Oxagen uses the hive: six hexagonal cells on a honeycomb grid, four drawn as an outline and two filled with the metal, one of them at half strength. It is the knowledge graph as a picture -- a lattice, with the parts Oxagen has learned lit up -- and it is built from five numbers, not drawn: a cell's height and width, the pitch along a row, the pitch between rows, and the outline's weight. The cells are a touch wider than a regular hexagon, which is what makes the cluster stand square.

The hive is two colours. Its outlines take the colour of the surface it sits on, and its two lit cells take the metal -- flat gold in the plain files, and the metal lit from above in the tiles. Do not add a third colour, do not fill the outlined cells, do not rotate it, and do not move a cell.

At 16 to 48 px both icons survive as themselves, and neither is redrawn to get there. The hive is six cells on a grid, which is what a 16 px grid can hold; only its outline is thickened, so the ink cells do not fall between pixels. The fill fraction goes up too -- at 16 px the mark takes almost the whole square, because the padding a 256 px tile wants is four pixels a favicon cannot spare. The small PNGs come from a favicon tile on ink, because an outline on nothing is no favicon on a tab that happens to be its colour.

Colour

Palette

The gold is #D4AF37, and its two neighbours are derived from it in OKLCH, not picked: gold-bright is lighter, for the moment the shimmer passes, and gold-deep is darker and a few degrees warmer, for gold set as text on white. The build fails if a pinned value stops matching its derivation. gold clears 9.5:1 on obsidian; on white it is 2.1:1, which is why gold as text on white becomes gold-deep at 4.7:1.

L 0.86 · C 0.130 · H 91°

L 0.56 · C 0.100 · H 92°

  • One gold action per screen. The focus ring is gold too, because it marks where that action is.
  • Gold is never a state, a surface fill, a card border, or a row highlight. If a screen shows two gold things that are not the mark, one of them is wrong.
  • Gold is flat. The sheen is only for the mark at hero sizes and on the icon tiles. Gold is never translucent, never blurred, and never a shadow.

Grounds

Dark comes first. Obsidian is the ground, a panel sits one step up, and a lifted row one step above that. The light theme is white, and a card on white is a hairline border, not a tint. The greys are neutral zinc with no hue, so the gold is the only warm colour on a screen. Every page ships both themes.

Text

Text comes in four roles. Each role has one value on ink and one on paper. Every role that carries meaning clears 4.5:1 on its ground, and the build checks it. On a lifted row in the light theme, secondary text moves to --ox-muted-text-ink (#6E6E77, 4.6:1), because #71717A is 4.4:1 there.

State

A state is shown by border shape first, so it still reads in grayscale, in print, and in either theme. Colour backs the shape up. It is never the only signal.

Heldalso allowed and proven: a double border
Pendingalso approval: a dashed border
Brokenalso denied and failed: a single border

Inside a table, a border is too small to read, so a state becomes a badge. The dot is the state's mark, which needs 3:1. The word takes the state's text stop, which clears 4.5:1 on the ground, a panel, and a lifted row. On paper each text stop equals its mark today. Use the text stop anyway, so a word stays readable when a mark moves.

Typography

Typefaces

Mac set one type rule on 2026-10-02. Aeonik sets the default text on every surface: body, labels, buttons, tables, and navigation. It also sets h1 to h3 in the web app and the internal tools, and every h4 to h6 everywhere. Its italic ships beside it. Space Grotesk sets h1 to h3 on the marketing and customer sites, and the docs sites count as customer sites. It also sets the two wordmarks, and that use is fixed. Its wide geometric letters lose their shape below 20px. At the shipped base, every heading step that can take it is 20px or more, and the theme editor warns when one falls under 20px. Monaspace Neon sets code, logs, digests, paths, ids, and the numbers in tables, with texture healing and code ligatures on.

Aeonik Mono and Aeonik Fono load too, so a page can name them. No role reads them yet.

Scales

A surface picks one scale and keeps it. marketing (text-m-*) is large and spaced, for a landing page or a post read once. app (text-a-*) is dense, for the web app, panels, tables, and logs.

Each scale has one base, its body size. The base is 16px on marketing and customer sites, docs included, and 14px in the web app and the internal tools. Mac's rule: "The base page font size should never be lower than 14px."

Every other step is the base times its ratio. For example, the app micro step is calc(var(--ox-a-base) * 0.857143). Change the base in theme/theme.json or the theme editor, and every step on that scale follows.

The steps under the base are for labels, badges, timestamps, and table headers. At the shipped base, app micro is 12px, app 2xs is 10px, and marketing micro is 14px. Running text, buttons, inputs, menu items, and table cells use the base.

Nothing is hard-coded. Every size reads a step token, such as --ox-a-micro, or a house utility, such as text-a-micro. build/css_literals.py fails a hard-coded font size, such as 13px or 0.8rem.

Tracking

Tracking is the space between letters. Headings track tighter as they grow, so large type does not look loose. Smaller headings and body text are not tracked, and neither are the wordmarks.

Type rules

  • Headings use sentence case. Capitalise the first word and proper names only.
  • No fourth role face. A CSS rule names a role, such as --font-display or --font-mono, never a face, so a face can change in one place.
  • An eyebrow is Aeonik on the app micro step, uppercase, at 0.14em tracking. An eyebrow is the small label above a heading, like the word above each heading on this page. The micro step is 12px at the shipped base.
  • Numbers in tables use Monaspace Neon. Every digit is the same width, so columns of figures line up.
  • Monaspace Neon keeps texture healing and code ligatures on (font-feature-settings: "calt", "liga"). Texture healing evens out the space around narrow and wide letters. Ligatures join pairs such as => into one glyph.

Font files

tokens/house-fonts.css carries the @font-face rules for every face in fonts/. tokens/next-fonts.ts loads them with next/font in a Next.js app. tokens/house-tailwind.css carries both scales as Tailwind v4 utilities. fonts/README.md lists every font file.

Elements

Other elements

Three more properties finish every surface: corner radius, shadow, and translucency. One rule ties them together. A surface at rest on the page is flat: a hairline border, almost no shadow, and a solid fill. Only a surface that floats above the page, such as a menu or a dialog, gets a deep shadow and a see-through fill.

Corner radius

On the website, cards, panels, and inputs round their corners at 12px (--ox-radius).

The app uses a scale instead. Each step multiplies one base value, --ox-radius-base, which is 0.45rem (about 7px). Change the base in theme/theme.json, and every corner in the app moves with it. Oxagen ADR-221 records the scale.

rounded-sm4px, base × 0.6a checkbox, a small chip
rounded-md6px, base × 0.8a badge, a bare text input, a skeleton
rounded-lg7px, base × 1a tooltip, an icon button, a toggle group
rounded-xl10px, base × 1.4an alert, a textarea, an empty state
rounded-2xl13px, base × 1.8a panel, a stat tile, a dialog, a menu row
rounded-3xl16px, base × 2.2a menu, a popover, a hover card, a toast
rounded-4xl19px, base × 2.6a button, a select, a form field
rounded-fullcirclea status dot, a switch, a radio, an avatar
  • A control you press or type into is a pill. Buttons, selects, and form fields use rounded-4xl. At 36px tall, 19px is more than half the height, so the ends are fully round.
  • A corner inside a corner is smaller by about the gap between them. That keeps the two curves close to parallel. A menu rounds at rounded-3xl (about 16px) and insets its rows by 4px, so each row takes rounded-2xl (about 13px).
  • A tile icon rounds at 20 on a 96 box. That is about a fifth of its side.

Shadows

A surface at rest gets its edge from a 1px border: --ox-border on ink and --ox-paper-border on paper. The kit allows one faint shadow at rest, --ui-shadow (0 1px 2px oklch(0.15 0 0 / 0.07)). Every Tailwind shadow step reads that one value, so a theme can turn them all off in one place.

A floating surface takes shadow-pop instead. Menus, popovers, hover cards, the command menu, dialogs, sheets, and toasts all float. The shadow is 0 25px 50px -12px: obsidian at 25% on paper and black at 60% on ink. A floating surface drops its border for pop-ring, a 1px ring of the text colour at 5% on paper and 10% on ink.

Never add a glow, a coloured shadow, or a text shadow, and never put a shadow on the mark.

Translucency

A translucent surface lets you partly see what is behind it. Glass belongs only on chrome that floats over content: menus, selects, comboboxes, popovers, hover cards, the command menu, toasts, a dialog's scrim, and sticky navigation and header bars. Cards, panels, tables, and text never take it.

  • A floating surface fills at 70% of its panel colour. The browser blurs whatever is behind it by 40px and raises its saturation to 150%. The page shows through as soft colour, never as text you could read.
  • A sticky bar fills at 72% of the page colour. The website's nav and the app's header blur what scrolls under them by 24px at 150% saturation. Text set on the bar takes the primary text colour, which stays above 8:1 whatever passes under it.
  • Every glass surface has an opaque fallback. A browser with no backdrop-filter, or a reader who asks for reduced transparency, gets the same surface opaque on its own ground. A scrim keeps its dim and drops its blur.
  • A dialog sits on a scrim. The scrim is the dark layer that covers the page behind a dialog: near-black at 50% on paper and black at 60% on ink, with a 3px blur.
  • A wash marks a row. A hovered or highlighted row is the text colour at 10%. A state badge or alert sits on its state colour at 10 to 12%.
  • Secondary text on ink may use opacity. White at 60% takes the tone of the surface under it. It must still clear 4.5:1.
  • Gold is never translucent. The mark and the one gold action stay solid on every surface.

This page's top bar uses the same idea: the page colour at 88% with a 14px blur, so content scrolls under it without clashing.

Motion

The shimmer

The house motion is the shimmer: a band of light crosses the mark every 2.8 seconds. Stella's asterisk turns a sixth of a turn, its own symmetry, as the light passes over its gold. The hive takes the same band over all of it: its outline is held at a third strength and the band brings it up to full, and its two cells catch the highlight as the band crosses them. Same band, same tilt, same easing -- one gesture, made in hue on the metal and in brightness on the ink. All of it is CSS inside the SVG; it runs in an <img> with no script, and prefers-reduced-motion lands it on a still mark at full strength.

Surfaces

Composition

A surface is a ground, one bloom of the metal, the brand's own icon placed off-centre, and at most a few lines of type. When a surface needs more than a mark, it builds the picture out of the mark. Every surface below is the vector the kit ships, not a screenshot.

Wallpapers

graph scatters nodes across the ground, wires each to its two nearest neighbours, and runs gold edges from the mark out to the nodes nearest it: the one-to-many, drawn. blocks rebuilds the mark from blocks on a grid, each tile a shade brighter or deeper than the next, with a bloom of fainter blocks around it. orbit hangs five rings of nodes off the mark, each node wired inward to the ring inside it. glow and quiet are the mark alone, as a bloom and as a hairline -- and both are pulled back inside the canvas rather than cropped, because a mark clipped by a few per cent of its width reads as a mistake and not as a crop. word and echo carry the wordmark and no icon. word is the wordmark alone over its bloom. echo stacks the wordmark above and below itself, each copy fainter than the last and in the surface's ink alone, so the gold stays on the one word that is the mark. Every node is placed by a seeded random, so the same file comes out of every build.

Social

Ads

Every ad takes its copy from an approved, launch-released entry in messages/ads/ or messages/always-on/, and build/messages.py --check fails on any file in ads/ that no entry produces. The Oxagen campaign follows the operator's job. The workforce ad states the job, and each of the others explains one decision an operator makes: which agent has the authority to do what, how each agent is equipped, which agent spent what, and why the agent does not hold the keys. A short form keeps the scope of its long form, so the banner still says governed, recorded, or mediated where the poster does. The 300×250 drops the kicker and the call to action, because neither fits at a legible size, but it keeps the answer line in a shorter form. A held campaign, such as completion checks for bounded tasks, is written and not rendered until its capability ships. Stella runs two lines: the proof rule, and the green check. The always-on campaign adds three ads from messages/always-on/: night shift, capacity, and driver seat. Each ships in the four sizes, on ink and on paper.

Four of the five Oxagen campaigns take the ghost in the top right. The workforce ad takes the orbit instead, laid back behind the type: rings of nodes wired inward to one mark is the only composition the kit already owns that reads as many agents under one control plane. It is not a new shape; it is the wallpaper's, at ad scale and at ad strength.
